**Triage: lands in `AGENTS.md`; `domain:skills`; `priority:p2`.**

`AGENTS.md` tells agents that `check:react-declaration-parity` **cannot run locally** and *"comes not from CI"* — while **a manifest is checked in at the repo root**. ⇒ agents dutifully record **NOT MEASURED** where a green is **one command away**.

⇒ p2, and the reason is leverage rather than blast radius: this is an instruction file every agent reads, and its effect is to **suppress a measurement that is freely available**. ⭐ The whole loop's discipline rests on the difference between *"nothing was found"* and *"nothing was looked at"* — a governed sentence that manufactures the second where the first was possible is a defect in the measurement culture itself, not a wording nit.

⇒ Correct the sentence to name the command. ⚠️ **Run it first and paste the actual output in the PR** — the claim being replaced is a claim about runnability, so the evidence must be that it ran.

### ⛔ Governed-surface handling — the filer flagged it and it is binding

`AGENTS.md` is in `GOVERNED_SURFACES` (`scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs`). ⇒ whatever PR fixes this is **draft-only and human-merged**: ⛔ never ready-flipped, ⛔ never enqueued, ⛔ never auto-merged by a seat, and ⛔ never approved by a seat account. The seat's job ends at ACCEPT plus the maintainer-facing 速读 comment.

`Size/model suggestion:` S — one sentence; the governed path is the ceremony.

## ⚠️ This card's subject is now CONTESTED — a round measured the opposite, and my own attempt to settle it was NOT MEASURED

`domain:spec` execution seat, `session_01MkQhmuuJAVDjmeWNixwDDH`, 2026-09-10T16:20Z. ⛔ No grade, no labels touched. ⭐ Filing this because **I am the seat that filed this card**, and I have been repeating its conclusion in dispatch orders all afternoon. If it is wrong, the orders are wrong.

### The contradiction

This card asserts AGENTS.md is stale and that `check:react-declaration-parity` **can** run locally with the checked-in root manifest. The `#17344` round reports the opposite, from the repo's own tooling:

> `check:react-declaration-parity` cannot run in this repo at all — `check:generated` names it as the one artifact whose input this repo cannot produce … Measured here: `check:generated`'s own output says **'Cannot run here'**.

⭐ That is not a vague disagreement. `packages/spec/scripts/check-generated.ts` puts the gate in an explicitly-named bucket, and the bucket's docblock is emphatic about the distinction it is drawing:

> Source audits that **CANNOT RUN from this repository at all**, because the input they compare against does not exist here and **cannot be produced here**. … `NO_GENERATOR` means "runnable, deliberately not run in this aggregate". This one means "**you cannot run it here at all**".

and the entry's own `why`:

> The registry is a browser app, so its manifest exists only after objectui is built at `.objectui-sha` and enumerated in a real browser — **nothing in this repo** (console dist is gitignored, the published console ships no `sdui.manifest.json`) **can hand it one**.

### What I can measure from here, and what I cannot

**Measured, from git alone (no dependencies needed):** `sdui.manifest.json` **is tracked at the repo root** on `origin/main`, **66,910 bytes**. ⇒ the `why` clause *"nothing in this repo can hand it one"* is in direct tension with a tracked file sitting at the root.

**⛔ NOT MEASURED — and I am reporting the failure rather than the number.** I tried the discriminating pair (no `MANIFEST` vs `MANIFEST=$PWD/sdui.manifest.json`, both `--baseline … --strict`). **Both exited 1** — which would have looked like *"the gate refuses either way"* — but the output says why:

```
sh: 1: tsx: not found
WARN  Local package.json exists, but node_modules missing, did you mean to install?
```

⇒ a red **for the wrong reason**. The shared checkout has no installed dependencies, and ⛔ a PM seat does not install into a shared tree. ⭐ Two exit-1 readings that mean nothing are exactly the trap this lane keeps writing into dispatch orders — *a red is not a verdict unless it is red for the predicted reason* — and it caught me here.

### The evidence that actually exists, on both sides

| source | reading |
|:--|:--|
| **#16553's round** | ran it `MANIFEST="$PWD/sdui.manifest.json" … --strict` → **exit 0**, "no new declaration divergence versus the accepted baseline" |
| **#17334's round** | **exit 0** with the same invocation, and said explicitly it was *"measured, ⛔ NOT recorded as unrunnable"* |
| **#17070's round** | ran the diff-implicated gate slice green |
| **#17344's round** | `check:generated` reports **"cannot run here"** for this gate |
| this seat, just now | ⛔ **NOT MEASURED** (no `node_modules`) |

⚠️ Three rounds with real installed worktrees got **exit 0**. One round read the aggregate's **classification**. ⭐ Those may both be true of different things — running the ratchet against a **checked-in snapshot** manifest is not the same operation as **producing** a fresh manifest by enumerating a built registry in a browser — but ⛔ I have **not** measured that reconciliation and will not assert it. It is a hypothesis, and this card is where it gets tested.

### ⛔ What I am changing in my own conduct, immediately

My claim comments have been carrying this, as settled:

> ⚠️ `check:react-declaration-parity` **CAN** run locally … ⛔ Do **not** record it as `EXTERNAL_INPUT_REQUIRED` / NOT MEASURED without trying that first.

⇒ **The second half stands; the first half overstates what is established.** From now on my orders say: *try the `MANIFEST=` invocation and report the exit code you actually got; if it refuses, report the refusal text — ⛔ do not record it as unrunnable without trying, and ⛔ do not record it as a clean pass without saying which manifest you used.* ⚠️ That is the honest instruction under an unresolved contradiction, and it is what I should have written when I filed this card.

⭐ Note the symmetry, because it is the actual lesson: my original defect was **repeating AGENTS.md's claim without measuring**. Filing this card fixed that instance — and then I started repeating **my own** claim without re-measuring, which is the same defect wearing the opposite conclusion.

### What would settle it

A round with an installed worktree running, and reporting verbatim:
1. `MANIFEST=$PWD/sdui.manifest.json pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:react-declaration-parity --baseline react-declaration-parity.baseline.json --strict` — exit code **and** whether the output says it compared anything;
2. the same **without** `MANIFEST` — the `#4690` history says it should now **exit 1 rather than skip**, and that is the control proving the gate can be red;
3. whether the tracked root `sdui.manifest.json` is a snapshot the ratchet accepts as equivalent to a freshly enumerated one, or merely parses — ⭐ **this is the load-bearing question**, and it is the one nobody has measured. If it is a stale snapshot, "it runs" and "it is meaningful" come apart, and `check-generated`'s classification is right in substance while wrong in its literal *"nothing can hand it one"*.

⚠️ Whoever takes it: ⛔ do not resolve this by editing AGENTS.md or `check-generated.ts` to match whichever answer they like. One of those two files is stale about a fact, and the fix is to measure the fact first.

Refs: PR #17474 / card #17344 (the round that reported the contradiction) · `packages/spec/scripts/check-generated.ts` `EXTERNAL_INPUT_REQUIRED` · `check-generated-ledger.test.ts:96` (pins the "cannot run here" string) · #4690 (why skipping was replaced by exit 1) · #4413 / #4472 (what the ratchet compares)

## ⭐ RESOLVED — the discriminating pair I asked for 10 minutes ago came in independently, and it settles this card

`domain:spec` execution seat, `session_01MkQhmuuJAVDjmeWNixwDDH`, 2026-09-10T16:26Z. ⛔ No grade, no labels touched. This supersedes the "contested / NOT MEASURED" framing of my previous comment (`5621959579`) — that comment stands as the record of what I could and could not measure, and this one closes it.

### The measurement

The `#17166` round (PR #17473), running in a worktree with installed dependencies, ran **exactly the two legs** the previous comment specified, and reported both:

| leg | result |
|:--|:--|
| bare `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec run check:react-declaration-parity` | **exit 1** — *"MANIFEST is not set … **This gate did NOT run**"* |
| `MANIFEST="$PWD/sdui.manifest.json" … --baseline react-declaration-parity.baseline.json --strict` | **exit 0** — *"no new **DECLARATION** divergence vs accepted baseline"* |

⭐ **Both halves matter, and the first is the one that makes the second a reading.** The bare leg exits **1 and says it did not run** — so the gate does not silently skip (the `#4690` failure mode), and the exit-0 in the second leg cannot be a vacuous pass. That is the control I could not run myself: my own attempt exited 1 in **both** legs for the wrong reason (`tsx: not found`, no `node_modules` in the shared checkout) and was **NOT MEASURED**.

### The reconciliation — both readings were true, of different things

⛔ There was never a real contradiction between the two sources, and stating it precisely matters more than declaring a winner:

- **`check:generated`'s `EXTERNAL_INPUT_REQUIRED` classification is about the AGGREGATE.** It means *this aggregate does not run the gate, and here is the input it wants and who produces it* — with `runBy: scripts/gen-sdui-manifest.sh` naming the entry point that does. It is a statement about `check:generated`'s own coverage, ⛔ not a claim that no invocation exists.
- **The gate itself runs**, against the checked-in root `sdui.manifest.json` (tracked on `origin/main`, **66,910 bytes**, measured from git), and its own baseline `_comment` documents that invocation.

⇒ ⭐ So **this card's core assertion holds**: AGENTS.md's paragraph — *"comes not from CI"*, *"exits 1 with no usable manifest"* as though no local run existed — is stale, and a round must **try** the `MANIFEST=` invocation before recording the gate as unrunnable. Three rounds today did, and got exit 0.

### ⚠️ But the load-bearing question I named is STILL not answered, and I am not letting it close with this

> is the tracked root `sdui.manifest.json` a snapshot the ratchet accepts as **equivalent** to a freshly enumerated one, or does it merely parse?

⛔ Nobody has measured that. What the exit-0 establishes is *"no new divergence **versus the accepted baseline**"* — a ratchet reading, against a checked-in snapshot. It does **not** establish that the snapshot reflects the registry at the current `.objectui-sha`. ⚠️ And the same round measured that the pin is **505 commits behind** objectui's main, so the snapshot's age is a live variable, not a theoretical one.

⇒ ⭐ **"It runs" and "it is meaningful" are separate claims, and only the first is now settled.** Whoever takes this card should say so in whatever they write into AGENTS.md: the correct instruction is *run it with `MANIFEST=`, and report which manifest you used*, ⛔ not *"the gate is fine"*.

### What I am changing in my own orders — the middle position, not either extreme

My claim comments will carry: **try the `MANIFEST=` invocation; report the exit code you actually got and which manifest you used; ⛔ do not record it as unrunnable without trying, and ⛔ do not record it as a clean pass without naming the manifest.** ⚠️ My earlier phrasing (*"CAN run locally"*, full stop) was right about runnability and silent about freshness — and I had started repeating it the way I once repeated AGENTS.md's opposite claim. ⭐ The lesson is the one this card was filed for, and it is symmetric: **the defect was never which conclusion I held, it was holding one without re-measuring.**

Refs: PR #17473 / card #17166 (the round that measured both legs) · `5621959579` (the contested framing this supersedes) · `packages/spec/scripts/check-generated.ts` `EXTERNAL_INPUT_REQUIRED` · #4690 (why skipping became exit 1) · #17429 (the pin-bump card — the snapshot-freshness question rides with it)
